title: The Full Newton–Girard Recurrence over Any Number of Variables
description: The parent chain (amgm-inequality-oq-02) studies elementary symmetric polynomials and power sums. Its OQ-02-OQ-01-OQ-01 asks for the full Newton–Girard recurrence pₖ = Σᵢ (−1)ⁱ⁻¹ eᵢ pₖ₋ᵢ in any number of variables. A gallery sibling proved this for three quantities by hand; Mathlib proves the identities in full generality over MvPolynomial σ R (mul_esymm_eq_sum, psum_eq_mul_esymm_sub_sum). This entry packages those as the general Newton–Girard recurrence — the eₖ recurrence, the power-sum recurrence, the closure relation at k = |σ|, and the base case p₁ = e₁ — with 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext:
Newton's identities (the Newton–Girard formulae) relate the power sums pₖ = Σᵢ xᵢᵏ of a collection of variables to their elementary symmetric polynomials eₖ. The power-sum form, pₖ = e₁ pₖ₋₁ − e₂ pₖ₋₂ + ⋯ + (−1)ᵏ⁻¹ k eₖ, recursively computes every power sum from the elementary symmetric polynomials, and is the computational core of the classical theory of symmetric functions (and of Galois theory, via the relation between roots and coefficients). Albert Girard stated them in 1629; Newton developed them around 1666–1683.

A gallery sibling proved the recurrence by hand for three quantities. Mathlib, however, proves Newton's identities in full generality over the multivariate polynomial ring MvPolynomial σ R for any finite index type σ and commutative ring R, via Zeilberger's involutive combinatorial proof (mul_esymm_eq_sum for the eₖ form, psum_eq_mul_esymm_sub_sum for the pₖ form). This entry packages those as the general Newton–Girard recurrence, recording the eₖ recurrence, the power-sum recurrence (the OQ's target), the closure relation when k reaches the number of variables, and the base case p₁ = e₁.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the full Newton–Girard recurrence for power sums in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials, for any number of variables: pₖ = (−1)^{k+1} k eₖ − Σ_{i+j=k, 0<i<k} (−1)ⁱ eᵢ pⱼ (equivalently pₖ = Σᵢ (−1)ⁱ⁻¹ eᵢ pₖ₋ᵢ). Record the eₖ recurrence, the closure at k = |σ|, and the base case p₁ = e₁.
overview.proofStrategy: Each result is the corresponding Mathlib theorem restated in gallery form: newton_esymm_recurrence = mul_esymm_eq_sum (the eₖ recurrence), newton_psum_recurrence = psum_eq_mul_esymm_sub_sum (the pₖ recurrence), newton_sum_zero = sum_antidiagonal_card_esymm_psum_eq_zero (closure at k = |σ|). The base case psum_one_eq_esymm_one rewrites p₁ and e₁ to their common value Σᵢ Xᵢ via psum_one and esymm_one.
keyInsights: Newton's identities hold over an arbitrary commutative ring and any number of variables — they are formal/combinatorial, not analytic facts about complex roots.
The power-sum recurrence pₖ = (−1)^{k+1} k eₖ − Σ_{0<i<k} (−1)ⁱ eᵢ pₖ₋ᵢ computes every pₖ from e₁,…,eₖ and lower power sums, with the base case p₁ = e₁.
When k reaches the number of variables |σ|, the recurrence closes: the full alternating sum Σ_{i+j=k} (−1)ⁱ eᵢ pⱼ vanishes, since eᵢ = 0 for i > |σ|.
The antidiagonal indexing {i + j = k} with the filter 0 < i < k is the precise bookkeeping of the cross terms eᵢ pₖ₋ᵢ in the recurrence.
Mathlib's general proof (Zeilberger's sign-reversing involution on pairs) supersedes the hand-rolled three-variable derivation, giving the identity uniformly for all σ and R.
prerequisites: Elementary symmetric polynomials and power sums in MvPolynomial

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 67 lines and 4 theorems packaging the full Newton–Girard recurrence over MvPolynomial σ R for any finite σ and commutative ring R: the eₖ recurrence, the power-sum recurrence pₖ = (−1)^{k+1} k eₖ − Σ_{i+j=k, 0<i<k} (−1)ⁱ eᵢ pⱼ, the closure relation at k = |σ|, and the base case p₁ = e₁.
conclusion.implications: This answers the parent's OQ-02-OQ-01-OQ-01 in full generality — the Newton–Girard recurrence for any number of variables — generalizing the gallery's hand-proved three-variable case (solution-of-cubic-oq-03-oq-04) by invoking Mathlib's combinatorial development. The recurrence is the computational bridge between symmetric-function data (eₖ) and power-sum data (pₖ), central to the roots↔coefficients dictionary and to symmetric-function identities throughout algebra.
openQuestions: Specialize the general recurrence to concrete small k (k = 2, 3, 4) by evaluating the filtered antidiagonal sums, recovering the textbook identities p₂ = e₁² − 2e₂, p₃ = e₁³ − 3e₁e₂ + 3e₃, etc.
Invert the recurrence over a ℚ-algebra to express eₖ as polynomials in p₁,…,pₖ, giving the dual Newton–Girard formulae.
